title: H4682 (123rd General Assembly): Selling or giving of firearms

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2019-11-20; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess123_2019-2020/prever/4682_20191120.htm (LegiScan doc 2070287))
provenance.note: Introduced version (Nov. 20, 2019); no later version or vote on file. Struck: old penalty tiers (up to $2,000 / 5 years; misdemeanor up to $1,000 / 1 year for Section 16-23-20) and the old stand-alone definitions in 16-23-210 (re-added as new text).

operative_text:
Section 6 (new Section 23-31-910): (A) It is unlawful to sell or give a firearm to a person whose name appears on the consolidated terrorist watch list maintained by the Terrorist Screening Center administered by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
Section 6 (new Section 23-31-910): (B) A person who knowingly sells or gives a firearm to a person in violation of subsection (A) is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction, must be fined not more than fifty thousand dollars or must be imprisoned for a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of ten years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted, and not more than twenty years, or both.
Section 4 (Section 16-23-230): It is unlawful for a person to store, keep, possess, or have in possession or permit another to store, keep, possess, or have in possession a machine gun or firearm commonly known as a machine gun, military firearm, sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, or assault weapon, except as provided in Sections 16-23-250 and 23-31-330.
Section 5 (Section 16-23-240): It is unlawful for a person to sell, rent, give away, or participate in any manner, directly or indirectly, in the sale, renting, giving away, or otherwise disposing of a machine gun, or firearm commonly known as a machine gun, military firearm, sawed-off shotgun, sawed-off rifle, or assault weapon, except as provided in Sections 16-23-250 and 23-31-330.
Section 1 (Section 16-23-50): (A) A person, including a dealer, who violates the provisions of this article, except Section 16-23-20, is guilty of a felony and, upon conviction: (1) for a first offense, must be fined not more than fifty thousand dollars or imprisoned not more than ten years, or both; and (2) for a second or subsequent offense, must be fined not more than fifty thousand dollars or imprisoned for a mandatory minimum term of imprisonment of ten years, no part of which may be suspended nor probation granted, and not more than twenty years, or both.
